\title{Asymptotic Dictionary Correction Discovery:\\ A Deterministic, Identifiability-Aware Framework\\

\begin{abstract}
Many physical laws take the form ``a known classical formula plus a small correction''
(for example, relativistic time dilation).
We present \textbf{ADCD} (Asymptotic Dictionary Correction Discovery), a method that
searches for such a correction in noisy data.
It differs from general-purpose symbolic regression in three ways:
(i)~each building block of the correction is written so that it is exactly zero in the
classical limit, which avoids floating-point error;
(ii)~dimensional analysis proposes the dimensionless variables automatically; and
(iii)~a small table of physics-based function families restricts what is searched.
ADCD then returns one of two verdicts: IDENTIFIABLE (the data support the discovered
structure) or WITHHELD (they do not).
On three synthetic tests with 1\% noise, ADCD recovers the Screened Coulomb correction
exactly ($\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=30.65$), recovers the Entropy Expansion correction at the
level of its function family ($\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=14.70$; borderline, 2 of 5 noise seeds),
and withholds judgment on Time Dilation at $v\le0.3c$, where measurement noise alone
already accounts for $\mathrm{NMSE}\approx0.41$, far above our 0.05 acceptance threshold.
Results are reproducible given the same software and random seed.

\vspace{0.3em}
\noindent\textbf{Keywords:} symbolic regression; correction discovery;
dimensional analysis; structural prior; model selection; identifiability
\end{abstract}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Introduction}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

In the expanding landscape of machine learning for the physical sciences~\cite{carleo2019,wang2023},
physical laws frequently take a correction-first form: a known classical baseline
extended by a term that vanishes at the classical
limit~\cite{einstein1905,debye1923,callen1985}.
Recovering that correction from observational data is distinct from full equation
discovery: the baseline is fixed, only the residual must be identified, and that
residual must vanish exactly where classical physics holds.

\paragraph{A concrete example.}
Coulomb's law gives an electrostatic force that falls off as $1/r^2$. In a simple phenomenological screening model, charges screen
each other and the measured force falls off faster: $F = (k_e q_1 q_2 / r^2) e^{-r/\lambda_D}$.
Given noisy measurements and the classical formula, ADCD returns the correction
$\theta_0(e^{-r/\theta_4}-1)$, where the fitted length $\theta_4\approx1.49$~m is close
to the true Debye length (1.50~m).
Just as important, when the data are too noisy to support any conclusion, ADCD says so
instead of returning its best guess.

General-purpose symbolic regression engines such as PySR~\cite{cranmer2020,cranmer2023},
AI Feynman~\cite{udrescu2020}, and PhySO~\cite{tenachi2023} excel at open-ended equation discovery from scratch.
However, when repurposed directly to find small asymptotic corrections to an established law,
unconstrained search encounters three practical hurdles:
(i)~\emph{numerical cancellation}: near the classical limit $u\to0$, standard representations
suffer loss of floating-point significance~\cite{ieee754};
(ii)~\emph{run-to-run variability}: stochastic optimization may return different Pareto candidates across random seeds~\cite{bongard2007,schmidt2009}; and
(iii)~\emph{uncalibrated confidence}: returning a single best-fit expression without quantifying whether the residual signal exceeds the noise floor risks presenting an unverified expression as a physical law~\cite{lacava2021,messeri2024,krenn2022}.
ADCD is designed specifically for this correction-first regime: algebraically regularized primitives
eliminate numerical cancellation; deterministic grammar enumeration provides reproducible candidate evaluation;
and explicit identifiability gating reports when data cannot discriminate between candidate structures.

\paragraph{Contributions.}
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]
  \item \emph{Method.} A correction-first search whose building blocks vanish exactly in
        the classical limit, with dimensionless variables generated automatically.
  \item \emph{Verdicts.} An explicit IDENTIFIABLE / WITHHELD decision based on four
        checks, so the method reports when the data are not informative enough.
  \item \emph{Evidence.} Three synthetic scenarios (including one where ADCD correctly
        withholds), plus multi-seed and wrong-prior audits (Appendix~\ref{app:audits}).
\end{itemize}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Related Work}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

Automated scientific discovery traces back to pioneering heuristic systems such as
BACON~\cite{langley1987} and has evolved toward modern autonomous equation
discovery~\cite{kramer2026,makke2024,karagiorgi2022}.
General SR engines (Eureqa~\cite{schmidt2009}, PySR~\cite{cranmer2020,cranmer2023},
AI Feynman~\cite{udrescu2020,udrescu2020b}, PhySO~\cite{tenachi2023})
target unconstrained equation recovery and do not enforce classical-limit
constraints algebraically.
SINDy~\cite{brunton2016} shares our library-based approach but discovers
governing equations rather than corrections.
PINNs~\cite{raissi2019,karniadakis2021} embed physical laws as soft loss penalties;
ADCD imposes them as hard algebraic identities before any numerical computation.
Recent systems combining data with background knowledge and axiomatic reasoning,
such as AI-Descartes~\cite{cornelio2023} and AI~Hilbert~\cite{corywright2024},
highlight the importance of theory-grounded discovery, but do not address
catastrophic cancellation near asymptotic limits or provide formal identifiability gating.
While dimensional analysis and symmetry constraints have been integrated into
SR and dynamical learning~\cite{tenachi2023,petersen2021,otto2025},
ADCD extends this with a five-dimensional (MLT$\Theta$Q) dimensional grouping heuristic,
transcendental argument safety, and BIC-based identifiability reporting
in a single pre-fitting gate cascade.
By combining deterministic grammar enumeration, algebraic classical-limit enforcement,
phenomenon-specific functional priors, and explicit identifiability gating, ADCD provides a
principled, falsifiable workflow tailored to the correction-first paradigm.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Methods}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

\subsection{Problem formulation}

Let $y_\mathrm{obs}$ and $y_\mathrm{cl}$ be the observed target and classical
prediction. The correction residual is:
\begin{equation}
  \Delta =
  \begin{cases}
    y_\mathrm{obs}/y_\mathrm{cl} - 1 & \text{(multiplicative)} \\
    y_\mathrm{obs} - y_\mathrm{cl}   & \text{(additive)}
  \end{cases}
\end{equation}
To select between the two representations automatically, ADCD picks the form whose magnitude
correlates less with the classical baseline, measured by the absolute Spearman rank
correlation between $|y_\mathrm{cl}|$ and $|\Delta|$ (ties default to additive).
There is no numeric ambiguity threshold: additive mode is used by construction when
$\mathrm{std}(y_\mathrm{cl})<10^{-15}$ (a constant baseline), when fewer than 5 valid
points remain, or when both correlations vanish.
ADCD searches for $\hat{\Delta}(\mathbf{x};\boldsymbol{\theta})$ such that
$\hat{\Delta}\to0$ as the relevant dimensionless ratio $u\to0$.

\subsection{Algebraically regularized primitive dictionary}

Each primitive $D(u)$ satisfies $\lim_{u\to 0} D(u) = 0$ as an exact algebraic
identity by construction, while rationalizing subtraction-prone forms against catastrophic cancellation.
The reason is numerical: subtracting two nearly equal numbers wipes out significant digits,
so a correction that should be tiny but nonzero can round to exactly zero.
For example, the naive form $(1-u)^{-1/2}-1$ collapses to $0.0$ at
$u=10^{-16}$ in \texttt{float64}; the rationalized form
$u/[\sqrt{1-u}(\sqrt{1-u}+1)]$ returns $5.0\times10^{-17}$ at the same input.
Table~\ref{tab:primitives} lists all eight primitives.

$\lim_{u\to0}D(u)=0$ as an exact algebraic identity.
The first five are the core physics-motivated basis; the remaining three extend
coverage to oscillatory, saturation, and power-law regimes.
Column ``Physical origin'' cites the fundamental equation that produces this
functional family; it does not imply the primitive is restricted to that domain.}
\label{tab:primitives}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}lllp{3.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
Name & Regularized form $D(u)$ & Domain & Physical origin \\
\midrule
\texttt{D\_lor}      & $u/[\sqrt{1-u}(\sqrt{1-u}+1)]$ & $u\in[0,1)$ & Lorentz factor ($\gamma-1$) \\
\texttt{D\_rat}      & $u/(1-u)$                       & $u\neq 1$   & Yukawa/Fermi pole \\
\texttt{D\_exp}      & $e^{-u}-1$                      & all $u$     & Debye/Yukawa screening \\
\texttt{D\_log}      & $\ln(1+u)$                      & $u>-1$      & Entropy of mixing \\
\texttt{D\_sqrt\_inv}& $1/\sqrt{1+u}-1$                & $u>-1$      & Gravitational / Coulomb potential \\
\texttt{D\_pow}      & $|u|^{|\theta|}$                & $u\ge0$     & Power-law corrections \\
\texttt{D\_osc}      & $1-\cos u$                      & all $u$     & Wave / AC oscillatory \\
\texttt{D\_sat}      & $\tanh u$                       & all $u$     & Magnetic / sigmoid saturation \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Dimensional grouping and free-scale generation}
\label{sec:buckingham}

ADCD tracks the physical dimensions of every variable as a vector of integer exponents
over mass (M), length (L), time (T), temperature ($\Theta$), and electric charge (Q)
(note: uppercase $\Theta$ denotes temperature dimension, distinct from lowercase model parameters $\theta_k$).
Instead of solving the full dimensional-analysis problem, it uses a simple two-step
heuristic: first, it groups variables with identical dimensions into pairwise ratios
(e.g., $q_1/q_2$); second, it divides each dimensional variable by a free scale
parameter, linearly or quadratically ($v/\theta_{2k},\, v^2/\theta_{2k+1}$; e.g., $r/\theta_4$).
Charge is tracked separately so that two charges can form a dimensionless ratio; a
three-dimensional (MLT) engine would treat them as dimensionless scalars and skip this step.
In Screened Coulomb, four charge-related candidates are enumerated first, so the distance
ratio receives the index $\theta_4$. The index only reflects enumeration order; what
matters is that the fitted value lands near the true Debye length.

\subsection{Phenomenon-specific taxonomy as structural prior}
\label{sec:taxonomy}

Each physics phenomenon maps to a named set of permitted primitive families
derived exclusively from its fundamental equations.
For example, \texttt{yukawa\_debye\_screening} permits only \texttt{D\_exp}
and \texttt{D\_rat}: the Klein-Gordon equation yields $V\propto e^{-mr}/r$ and
Debye-H\"{u}ckel theory yields $\phi\propto e^{-r/\lambda_D}/r$; both involve
only exponential and rational families.
The taxonomy restricts \emph{which family} is searched; it says nothing about
\emph{which variable} enters the argument or \emph{what the scale is}---both
are determined by the dimensional grouping heuristic and numerical optimizer.
Allowing a function family that the physics does not justify gives the search an extra
flexible function that can soak up noise, which shrinks the ablation $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}$
gap and weakens identifiability.
Table~\ref{tab:taxonomy} lists entries for our three experiments.

A $3\times3$ cross-misspecification audit (Appendix~\ref{app:misspec},
Table~\ref{tab:app_misspec}) tests what happens when the wrong taxonomy is supplied.
In all 6 wrong-taxonomy trials the system returned WITHHELD, so there were no false
IDENTIFIABLE verdicts (the two Time Dilation trials fail the positive control under any prior; e.g., applying the oscillatory
\texttt{wave\_resonance} prior to Screened Coulomb yields WITHHELD with
$\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=-910.5$).\footnote{Full supplementary audit tables are provided in Appendix~\ref{app:audits} and at \url{https://github.com/apiprdt/PhysicsPaper/tree/PythonADCD/rebuttal}.}
In these tests, a wrong prior led to abstention rather than an invented law.

\subsection{Grammar enumeration and theta-intact constraint}

Candidates take the form $\hat{\Delta}=\theta_0\cdot D_i(u_{ij})$, optionally
extended with a secondary additive or multiplicative-coupled term ($\theta_0 D_a(u)+\theta_1 D_b(u)$ or $\theta_0 D_a(u)[1+\theta_1 D_b(u)]$; depth $\le3$, $\le25$ tokens).
Dimensionless arguments are auto-generated by the dimensional grouping heuristic
(up to 12 candidate ratios per scenario).
Gates~1--3 (Table~\ref{tab:gates}) inspect the symbolic \emph{theta-intact}
expression (where parameters $\theta_k$ remain symbolic without premature numerical substitution), treating single-variable free-scale ratios (e.g., $r/\theta_4$ representing a Debye length) as dimensionally admissible because $\theta_k$ absorbs the variable's physical scale during fitting.
Gate~4 (Asymptotic Regularization Check, ARC) evaluates the symbolic classical limit at $\boldsymbol{\theta}=\mathbf{1}$ (deferring parametric candidates for strict post-fit re-verification at $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$), and Gate~5 screens coarse numerical fitness at $\boldsymbol{\theta}=\mathbf{1}$.

\subsection{Physical gate cascade}
\label{sec:gates}

Before fitting, each candidate must pass a five-gate cascade
(Table~\ref{tab:gates}) applied to the theta-intact expression.

\begin{table}[ht]
\small
\caption{The five-gate pre-fitting physical cascade.}
\label{tab:gates}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{3.5cm}p{9cm}@{}}
\toprule
Gate & Rejection criterion \\
\midrule
1. AST complexity & SymPy tree depth $>12$ or token count $>50$. \\
2. Dimensional consistency & Physical dimensions mismatch target (allowing free-scale $v/\theta_k$). \\
3. Transcendental safety & Arguments to $\exp$, $\ln$, $\sqrt{\cdot}$ not dimensionless or $\theta_k$-scaled. \\
4. Asymptotic check (ARC) & Classical limit at $\boldsymbol{\theta}=\mathbf{1}$ (and post-fit $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}$) does not vanish. \\
5. Coarse numerical fitness & Evaluation at $\boldsymbol{\theta}=\mathbf{1}$ produces \texttt{NaN}/\texttt{Inf}. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Parameter optimization and model selection}

The top-ranked Stage-1 surviving candidates ($K=30$, shortlisted by coarse pre-fitting evaluation) are optimized via L-BFGS-B (JAX, \texttt{float64}).
Parameters are log-reparameterized ($\theta_i{=}s_i e^{u_i}$,
$s_i{\in}\{-1,+1\}$) for order-of-magnitude traversal; multiple restarts
reduce sensitivity to local optima.
Model selection uses an Extended BIC~\cite{schwarz1978,chen2008}: $\mathrm{BIC}=k\ln N - 2\ln\hat{L} + 2\ln|\mathcal{C}|$,
incorporating a multiple-testing penalty over the search space size $|\mathcal{C}|$.
By the Kass--Raftery scale~\cite{kass1995}, $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}>10$ is the
adopted identifiability threshold.

\subsection{Four-step validation protocol}
\label{sec:protocol}

\textbf{In plain terms.} IDENTIFIABLE means the data are informative enough to single out
the discovered function family. WITHHELD means they are not, so ADCD makes no structural
claim even if it found a good-looking fit.
An IDENTIFIABLE verdict requires all four checks to pass:
\begin{enumerate}[noitemsep,leftmargin=*]
  \item \textbf{Budget disclosure.} Before looking at results, we state how many candidate
        formulas are searched ($|\mathcal{C}|$) and which function families are allowed,
        so the size of the search is visible.
  \item \textbf{Positive control} (can the method recover the right answer at all?).
        Using only the true function family, the fit must explain at least 95\% of the
        variance in the data ($\mathrm{NMSE}<0.05$). If even the correct family fails,
        the data are too noisy to support a claim.
  \item \textbf{Ablation control} (is the family really needed?). We remove the target
        family and search over all remaining primitives. We require the domain-guided candidate to
        beat the best remaining model by $\Delta\mathrm{BIC} = \mathrm{BIC}_{\mathrm{ablated}} - \mathrm{BIC}_{\mathrm{domain}} > 10$
        (conventionally ``very strong evidence'', Kass--Raftery).
        Extended BIC balances deviance improvement against parameter parsimony, penalizing
        superfluous complexity when competing functional forms achieve comparable fit (Table~\ref{tab:app_bic}).
  \item \textbf{Determinism.} Three runs with identical inputs must give identical output.
\end{enumerate}
Failure of any check yields WITHHELD (in benchmark audits, Steps 2--3 evaluate against the known synthetic target family; in empirical deployment, Step~3 ablates the discovered candidate's family).

Two of three scenarios are IDENTIFIABLE; Time Dilation is WITHHELD because
its positive control fails within the historical $v\le0.3c$ observation window.

\paragraph{Reading $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}$.}
BIC scores a model by how well it fits the data, with penalties for extra parameters and
for a larger search space.
$\Delta\mathrm{BIC}$ is the score of the best model \emph{without} the true family minus
that of the best model \emph{with} it, so larger values favor the domain-guided result and
values above 10 are conventionally called very strong evidence.
It has three parts (Appendix Table~\ref{tab:app_bic}): $\Delta D$, the pure difference in
fit; $\Delta k\ln N$, the reward for using fewer parameters; and a penalty for searching a
larger space.%
\footnote{$\Delta\mathrm{BIC}$ includes a search-space penalty
$2\ln|\mathcal{C}|$ that differs between domain-guided and ablated runs;
$\Delta D$ reports the penalty-free fit-quality difference.
Here $|\mathcal{C}_\mathrm{ablated}|=814/534/700$ for Screened Coulomb, Entropy
Expansion, and Time Dilation, versus $|\mathcal{C}_\mathrm{domain}|=60/40/10$.
Screened Coulomb's $\Delta D=20.14$ alone exceeds the
Kass--Raftery threshold of~10.
Entropy Expansion's identifiability is parsimony-driven
($\Delta D=-1.08$; the ablated model achieves an equivalent fit
with more parameters), as reported in Table~\ref{tab:results}.}
Reporting all three shows what drives each verdict.

\paragraph{Screened Coulomb.}
Recovered $\theta_0(e^{-r/\theta_4}-1)$ is an exact symbolic match to the
ground truth $\theta_0(e^{-r/\lambda_D}-1)$, with $\theta_4\approx1.49$~m
recovering the Debye length $\lambda_D=1.50$~m.
The engine selected the distance ratio $r/\theta_4$ on its own (the index reflects
enumeration order, as in Section~\ref{sec:buckingham}).
$\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=30.65$ far exceeds the threshold of~10, and $\Delta D=20.14$ shows
the advantage comes from fit quality, not from the search-space penalty.
Over 5 noise seeds the verdict is IDENTIFIABLE every time (5/5); $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}$
ranges from 11.0 to 263, and the mean of 76.61 is driven by one large value
(penalty-free $\overline{\Delta D + \Delta k\ln N}=71.39$).

\paragraph{Entropy Expansion.}
Because the classical baseline $S_i$ is constant, the scale-dependence test is
uninformative and mode detection falls back to an additive search. Thus, the recovered additive
correction $\theta_0\ln(1+dV/V_i)$ matches the additive ground truth
$nR\ln(1+dV/V_i)$ at class level: the fitted amplitude $\hat{\theta}_0 \approx 8.30\text{ J/K}$
absorbs the composite constant $nR = 8.314\text{ J/K}$ (within 0.2\%).
ADCD labels this match \texttt{class\_only}: the functional family $\ln(1+u)$ is correctly identified,
but because $n$ and $R$ are not individually supplied as variables to the search, the composite product $nR$
cannot be decomposed into separate physical factors.
$\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=14.70>10$ supports IDENTIFIABLE, but $\Delta D=-1.08$ shows the
evidence comes from \emph{simplicity}, not from a better fit: the ablated search matches
the fit with $k{=}3$ parameters, versus $k{=}1$ for the domain-guided model.
Over 5 noise seeds the verdict is borderline (2/5 IDENTIFIABLE,
$\overline{\Delta\mathrm{BIC}}=9.91\pm3.40$, sample SD), so the logarithmic correction
sits at the decision boundary under 1\% noise.

\paragraph{Time Dilation.}
Over $v/c\in[0.10,0.30]$, the Lorentz correction $\gamma-1$ peaks at $4.8\%$ with a signal standard deviation of $\mathrm{SD}(\Delta_\mathrm{true})\approx1.25\%$ against the $1.0\%$ measurement noise.
The grammar recovers the Lorentz structure $D_\mathrm{lor}(v^2/c^2)$ at
Rank~1 ($\hat{\theta}_0\approx1.01$), but the positive control fails ($\mathrm{NMSE}=0.41$).
Put simply, even the exact true curve would differ from the noisy data by about 41\% of
the data's variance ($\mathrm{NMSE}\approx0.412>0.05$), so no method could pass the 5\% test in this window; the Positive
Control correctly returns WITHHELD.
Over 5 noise seeds this verdict is stable (5/5 WITHHELD).

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Discussion}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

\textbf{Why withholding is a useful answer.}
A method that always returns a formula, whatever the data quality, cannot tell the reader
when to trust it. ADCD's WITHHELD verdict on Time Dilation marks the limit of the data:
lowering noise ($\sigma\lesssim0.29\%$) or widening the velocity window ($v\gtrsim0.5c$ at $\sigma=1\%$) reduces the noise floor below $0.05$, while separating $D_\mathrm{lor}$ from competing rational/polynomial families on pure fit ($\Delta D>10$) requires extending into the relativistic regime ($v>0.3c$).

\textbf{Taxonomy as prior, not hint.}
The taxonomy restricts \emph{which primitive family} is active;
the dimensional grouping heuristic and optimizer determine \emph{which variable}
and \emph{which scale} within that family.
This is by design: ADCD operates as a domain-guided framework
(see Table~\ref{tab:comparison}, row ``Prior''), not a tabula-rasa search.
The taxonomy prior is active from the budget-disclosure step onward,
consistent with the framework's explicit use of peer-reviewed functional
priors as a structural constraint.
In Screened Coulomb, the search, not the taxonomy, selected the distance variable and its
scale ($\theta_4\approx1.49$~m).
In the $3{\times}3$ misspecification audit, none of the 6 wrong-taxonomy trials produced a
false IDENTIFIABLE verdict.

\textbf{Comparison with general SR.}
ADCD and general SR address complementary objectives: discovering small corrections to an established baseline
vs.\ discovering full governing equations from scratch.
Unconstrained SR explores broad hypothesis spaces and constructs a Pareto frontier of complexity versus accuracy.
In contrast, ADCD formally tests whether observational data warrant a specific structural correction to a mature classical baseline.
Table~\ref{tab:comparison} summarises these complementary operational regimes.

\textbf{Principle-guided discovery.}
Recent perspectives on AI for physics stress that theory building needs compact laws,
symmetry, and controlled limits~\cite{shalyt2026}.
ADCD follows this spirit: it searches for a small correction anchored to an established
baseline and reports how strongly the data support it.

\begin{table}[ht]
\small
\caption{Complementary roles of ADCD and general-purpose symbolic regression.}
\label{tab:comparison}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{@{}p{2.8cm}p{3.5cm}p{4.2cm}@{}}
\toprule
Property & ADCD & General SR \\
\midrule
Target & Corrections to known laws & Full equations from scratch \\
Prior & Phenomenon-specific taxonomy & None (tabula rasa) \\
Dimensional engine & 5D MLT$\Theta$Q & Varies (often 3D or none) \\
Classical limit & Algebraic guarantee & Soft loss penalty \\
Identifiability & Explicit; WITHHELD if insufficient & Best-fit Pareto frontier \\
Reproducibility & Deterministic (fixed seed/env) & Stochastic (seedable) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\subsection{Limitations}
\label{sec:limitations}

\textbf{Weak-signal convergence.}
Time Dilation's positive control failure is the intended output when the
signal-to-noise ratio is too low.
Future work should investigate adaptive restarts and denser initialization grids.

\textbf{Scope.}
Current support covers eight primitive families, additive and multiplicative corrections, and
synthetic Gaussian noise.
Heavier-tailed noise and real observational data
(e.g., galactic rotation curves, pulsar timing residuals) remain future work;
real data require preprocessing for heteroscedastic uncertainties not yet modelled.
Validation thresholds ($\Delta\mathrm{BIC}>10$, $\mathrm{NMSE}<0.05$) were evaluated under $N=200$ and 1\% Gaussian noise; calibrating across broader noise regimes and sample sizes remains future work.

\textbf{Taxonomy coverage.}
Each new entry requires a peer-reviewed derivation for every admitted family---a
deliberate constraint preventing unchecked hypothesis-space expansion.

\textbf{Safety--expressivity trade-off.}
ADCD constrains its hypothesis space relative to general-purpose SR: candidates
failing dimensional consistency or outside the phenomenon-specific primitive set
are rejected before fitting.
This prevents fitting spurious mathematical complexity to observational noise, but means ADCD cannot discover corrections
whose functional family lacks a documented derivation.
The appropriate framing is complementarity: general SR explores broad hypothesis spaces from scratch;
ADCD audits targeted corrections to an already-established baseline.

\textbf{Seed stability of borderline verdicts.}
Entropy Expansion's verdict varies across noise realizations (2/5 IDENTIFIABLE,
3/5 WITHHELD), indicating the logarithmic correction sits at the identifiability
boundary under 1\% noise.
We treat this as a limitation of the current noise regime.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------
\section{Conclusion}
% ---------------------------------------------------------------

ADCD is a deterministic, correction-first framework combining algebraically
regularized primitives, 5D (MLT$\Theta$Q) dimensional grouping, and
a Phenomenon-Specific Taxonomy.
On three canonical scenarios, two yield IDENTIFIABLE results
(Screened Coulomb: $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=30.65$, exact match;
Entropy Expansion: $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}=14.70$, class-level, parsimony-driven)
and one yields a principled WITHHELD verdict (Time Dilation at $v\le0.3c$),
where the historical signal is insufficient for a confident structural claim.
Within its deliberate scope---known classical baseline, additive or multiplicative
correction, Gaussian noise---ADCD provides deterministic reproducibility and
explicit identifiability diagnostics, returning a principled WITHHELD verdict
(with its $\Delta\mathrm{BIC}$) when observational data cannot discriminate candidate structures.
We hope this work encourages broader adoption of explicit identifiability checks
and abstention mechanisms in scientific machine learning.

\subsection{Extended BIC Deviance and Penalty Decomposition}
\label{app:bic}

Under the Extended BIC formulation ($\mathrm{BIC} = k\ln N + N\ln\mathrm{NMSE} + 2\ln|\mathcal{C}|$), the ablation gap $\Delta\mathrm{BIC} = \mathrm{BIC}_{\mathrm{ablated}} - \mathrm{BIC}_{\mathrm{domain}}$ decomposes into pure fit quality ($\Delta D = N\ln(\mathrm{NMSE}_{\mathrm{ablated}}/\mathrm{NMSE}_{\mathrm{domain}})$), parameter parsimony ($\Delta k\ln N$), and search-space multiplicity ($2\ln(|\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{ablated}}|/|\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{domain}}|)$), as reported in Table~\ref{tab:app_bic} for $N=200$ ($\ln 200 \approx 5.30$, $\text{seed}=42$).

\subsection{Taxonomy Cross-Misspecification Safety Audit}
\label{app:misspec}

To verify that the phenomenon-specific taxonomy prior does not induce false discoveries when misspecified, each scenario was evaluated under its true physical taxonomy key and two intentionally mismatched keys that exclude the ground-truth primitive family. As shown in Table~\ref{tab:app_misspec}, all six misspecified trials returned \textbf{WITHHELD} (0/6 false discoveries): when the true primitive family is absent from the domain prior, the unrestricted ablation search outperforms the misspecified domain search ($\Delta\mathrm{BIC} \in [-1038.24, -674.62]$ on identifiable scenarios), triggering conservative abstention rather than overfitting.
